_comment: Verified display-number to bank-id map for SHOSMED_LF3_Chemistry_Batch6_Review.txt,
implemented 18 November 2026.
Unlike batches 1-5, this review SUPPLIES original identification signatures: a JSON
block giving each display number's ORIGINAL full stem, all four ORIGINAL option
texts, its topic and its answer letter. Verification therefore ran by FULL CONTENT
MATCH against the live bank, before any edit:
1. Each signature's original stem plus all four original option texts was matched
against every one of the 485 chemistry records, on a canonical form that
decodes HTML entities, strips tags, folds <sub>/<sup> and Unicode sub/superscripts
to plain digits, normalises dashes, quotes and Greek letters, and collapses
whitespace. All 60 matched EXACTLY ONE record each.
2. No two records anywhere in the 485-record chemistry bank share a full signature,
so no match is ambiguous and none had to be resolved by topic or answer pattern.
3. Each matched record's stored answer letter was cross-checked against the review's
letter for that display number: 60 of 60 agree, giving the review's own block
BBBBCBBDCB CBBBABCBCC BBBBCBBCBB CCBCCBBBBC CBBBBBBCBB BCBBCBCBBA and the
review's tally A=2, B=39, C=18, D=1.
4. Each record's stored topic was compared with the signature's topic: 60 of 60 agree.
Contiguity is a RESULT of that verification, not an assumption: the ids turn out to
occupy 60 consecutive bank positions, chem-302 .. chem-361.
No id in this pack appears in chemistry batches 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 (299 ids), so all 60
displays are newly reviewed unique ids.
Independently confirmed stored inventories, all matching the review:
210 educational points: individual five-point blocks in Q1-Q15 and 45 generic
three-point blocks in Q16-Q60. The generic blocks draw on only THREE stock sets of
three lines (x25, x10, x10 = 45 items).
0 Bottom Lines and 0 tables stored, and none added.
All 60 keyed headings are LETTERED. 239 of 240 headings agreed with their own option
before the pass; the single gap was Q28, which was MISSING its option B paragraph
altogether (179 feedback paragraphs instead of 180), exactly as the review reports.
Every main explanation is a SINGLE paragraph, so the supplied multi-sentence
replacements stay in one paragraph.
No HTML entities and no <sub>/<sup> tags are stored; the pack uses Unicode
subscripts (156), superscripts (36), Greek letters (106) and arrows (21).
Q8 (chem-309) and Q58 (chem-359) each end with a pre-existing empty
, preserved byte-for-byte.
Q32 maps to chem-333. Its stored explanation really did contain a malformed

'

A. 2 ATP:' - five

opens against four closes, paragraph
nesting depth 2 - which is the same record flagged as a pre-existing defect while
reviewing earlier batches, then left alone because it lay outside those packs. The
review's own Q32 instruction to inspect and repair a real malformed paragraph is
what brings it into scope, and this pass repairs it as part of Q32's rewrite.
